Create an efficacy stopping rule for a group sequential design

Source: R/stopping_rule_gsd.R
stopping_rule_gsd.Rd

Create a rule that stops a simulated group sequential trial for efficacy at an interim analysis, given the hypotheses rejected so far. The rule is one Boolean condition per interim analysis: when the condition for interim analysis k is true, the trial stops after analysis k and no hypothesis can be rejected at a later analysis. The final analysis always ends the trial, so it has no condition.

Usage

stopping_rule_gsd(condition)

Arguments

condition

The stopping condition, or one condition per interim analysis. To inject values from your R session, use rlang's injection operator !!. One of:

  • an expression, such as r1 && (r2 || r3), or a single string, such as "r1 and (r2 or r3)": one condition, applied at every interim analysis;

  • a call to list() with one expression or string per interim analysis, such as list(r1, r1 && (r2 || r3)), or a list of them injected with !!;

  • a character vector with one string per interim analysis, such as c("r1", "r1 and (r2 or r3)"), or one injected with !!.

Value

A multigrain_stopping_rule_gsd object made up of:

  • conditions: a list of the conditions, as language objects.

  • labels: the conditions deparsed to strings, for display.

  • m_min: the largest hypothesis index referred to by an r<i> symbol, the fewest hypotheses the rule can be used with.

  • n_interim: NULL for a single condition applied at every interim analysis, otherwise the number of conditions supplied.

Details

A condition is written using:

  • r1, r2, ..., rm: the indicator that hypothesis \(H_i\) has been rejected at the current interim analysis or at an earlier one;

  • the logical operators &&, || and ! (or the words and, or and not in a string);

  • comparisons (== != < <= > >=) and arithmetic (+ - * /), so that a count of rejections such as r1 + r2 + r3 >= 2 can be tested;

  • numeric or logical scalars, and parentheses.

Every condition must refer to at least one r<i>. Decision times (t1, ...) and discount tables, which a group sequential gain can use (see trial_success_gsd()), are not available to a stopping rule.

When the rule is applied

The rule does not store the number of hypotheses m or of analyses K; both are settled when it meets a multigrain_pvals_gsd object (see transform_pvalues_gsd()). The rule may then refer to no hypothesis beyond m. A single condition is recycled to each of the K - 1 interim analyses; otherwise one condition per interim analysis is needed. A list of K conditions is accepted with a warning: the final analysis always ends the trial, so its condition is dropped. With K = 1 there is no interim analysis, and a single condition is accepted and has no effect. The rule is evaluated once on every possible set of rejected hypotheses, 2^m sets per interim analysis, so it can be used with at most 16 hypotheses.

Stopping only removes rejections, so error control is unaffected: a stopped trial keeps the rejections it has already declared and declares none at a later analysis.

A trial that has rejected every hypothesis stops at that analysis whether or not a rule is supplied, as nothing is left to test.

Operator precedence

Operator precedence follows R's own rules. Parenthesise to make intent explicit: write r1 && (r2 || r3) rather than relying on && binding tighter than ||.

See also

trial_success_gsd() for the group sequential gain, transform_pvalues_gsd() for the p-values the rule is settled against.

Examples

# Stop at any interim analysis once H1 and at least one of H2 and H3 are
# rejected
stopping_rule_gsd(r1 && (r2 || r3))
#> <multigrain_stopping_rule_gsd>
#> Every interim: r1 && (r2 || r3)
#> Hypotheses referenced: up to r3

# One condition per interim analysis (K = 3): stop at the first interim
# once H1 is rejected, at the second only once H2 or H3 is rejected too
stopping_rule_gsd(list(r1, r1 && (r2 || r3)))
#> <multigrain_stopping_rule_gsd>
#> Interim 1: r1
#> Interim 2: r1 && (r2 || r3)
#> Hypotheses referenced: up to r3

# The first rule, written as a string
stopping_rule_gsd("r1 and (r2 or r3)")
#> <multigrain_stopping_rule_gsd>
#> Every interim: r1 && (r2 || r3)
#> Hypotheses referenced: up to r3

# Stop once at least two of three hypotheses are rejected
stopping_rule_gsd(r1 + r2 + r3 >= 2)
#> <multigrain_stopping_rule_gsd>
#> Every interim: r1 + r2 + r3 >= 2
#> Hypotheses referenced: up to r3
